title: Dual-cavity bandpass filter with ZnS/MgF2 on Daimon-20 substrate
scientific_hypothesis: A 22-layer dual-cavity structure with ZnS/MgF2 quarter-wave-based stacks can achieve simultaneous transmission peaks at 3.30 μm and 4.25 μm with suppression in the 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm bands when layer thicknesses are optimized.
design_principle: Fabry-Perot cavities formed by low-index spacer layers between high-reflectivity DBR mirrors create transmission bands at wavelengths determined by cavity optical thickness. Two cavities with different thicknesses produce two passbands. Index contrast between ZnS (~2.3) and MgF2 (~1.35) provides sufficient reflectivity for blocking bands with limited layer count.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | Daimon-20
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 22 layers (within 24-layer limit)
All layers are dielectric (ZnS and MgF2 are conventionally depositable)
Layer thicknesses should remain within practical deposition ranges (50-2000 nm)
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: ZnS has high refractive index (~2.2-2.4) and good transmission in 3-5 μm IR range
Recalled knowledge: MgF2 has low refractive index (~1.35-1.40) and is transparent in IR
Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stack reflectivity increases with number of pairs and index contrast
Recalled knowledge: Fabry-Perot cavity transmission peak wavelength scales with cavity optical thickness (n×d)
Recalled knowledge: Dual-band filters can be constructed by cascading two cavities with different optical thicknesses
Recalled knowledge: Daimon-20 is a CaF2 dataset with index ~1.42-1.43 in this wavelength range
expected_advantages: ZnS/MgF2 pair provides high index contrast for efficient blocking with fewer layers
22-layer design leaves margin within the 24-layer constraint for potential refinement
Dual-cavity topology is a standard approach for multi-band transmission filters
All materials are from the guaranteed_names list and should resolve without ambiguity
known_risks: Uncertain about exact refractive indices of ZnS and MgF2 at 3-5 μm wavelengths - actual values may differ from recalled ~2.3 and ~1.35
Uncertain about Daimon-20 substrate index dispersion in this range - recalled value may not match dataset
Uncertain whether 22 layers is sufficient to achieve required blocking levels in suppression bands - may need more pairs
Recalled that ZnS may have some absorption features near 4-5 μm that could affect CO2 band transmission - would need to verify against actual dataset
The topology assumes normal incidence; if actual system uses oblique incidence, performance will shift
No polarization specification in request - design assumes unpolarized or normal incidence where polarization effects are minimal
Quarter-wave center wavelength selection is uncertain - chose 3.3 μm as compromise but 4.25 μm cavity may need different reference
execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on Daimon-20 substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence from air side: ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, then Daimon-20 substrate. Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses individually to maximize transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm bands while minimizing transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm bands. No metal layers. Total layer count is exactly 22. Materials are zns and mgf2 from the material catalog. Substrate is Daimon-20. Incidence is from air side at normal incidence (0 degrees). Wavelength range of interest is 2500-5000 nm.
revision_reason: Repaired material name for substrate from ambiguous CaF2 to resolved Daimon-20 per registry requirements
